target.scope: Vintage (pre-~2005, ideally 80s/90s) tees and crewnecks from tool/trade brands: Milwaukee Electric Tools, Klein Tools, DeWalt, Snap-on, Mac Tools, Matco, CAT, Craftsman, Stihl, Husqvarna, Black & Decker, Bosch, Porter-Cable, Ingersoll-Rand, John Deere.
target.size: Men's L or XL only. 90s cuts run a size big — judge by pit-to-pit 22-24 in when stated; ask for measurements when not.
target.era: Authenticate by evidence, never the word 'vintage': single stitch (pre-~1996), period blanks (Screen Stars, Hanes 50/50, Jerzees grid, Tultex USA, K-Products, Swingster, All Sport, Delta, Stedman, Velva Sheen, Lee), Made in USA. Honduras/Nicaragua/Bangladesh = late-90s+.
hot: Any confirmed-vintage Klein Tools shirt/sweatshirt L/XL up to ~$75 (unicorn: ~3 vintage Klein tees exist on market, none L/XL)
Milwaukee Electric Tools 80s/90s tee <=$60 or crew <=$90, L/XL
Any single-stitch/pre-2000 tool-brand tee <=$30 or crew <=$50, L/XL
Named grails <=~$60: Sadler/Dotter DeWalt racing, Ernie Irvan / Davey Allison Mac Tools, 80s Screen Stars Snap-on
target.autoPass: Print-on-demand (Gildan/Bella+Canvas/Next Level, 'S + more' menus, Located in Indonesia); brand retro reissues (Klein Est.1857/150th, Snap-on Faded USA Made/Retro Racing, Milwaukee 1924 heritage); listings hiding the tag; parody prints. DeWalt era: Sadler/Dotter=mid-90s, Kenseth #17 Chevy=1998-99, Kenseth #17 Ford=2000s (not 90s despite titles), Kenseth #20=modern. Kurt Busch was never DeWalt.
target.priceGuide: Niche tiers (asks, no sold comps yet): $5-40 common / $40-100 good / $130-700 grail. OBO listings likely close 10-25% under ask.

channels.notes: eBay/Etsy/Grailed/Depop/Mercari 403 plain WebFetch — use browser pane; Mercari and Facebook need real Chrome. Depop prices include buyer fees. Grailed is a markup market: find the piece there, buy it on eBay/Mercari. Gem (gem.app) aggregates everything incl. indie shops. Facebook Marketplace not yet swept for this hunt.
